Joints
Individual Variety

Brassica rapa

Bok Choy

35–53 mg Vitamin C + 2.6 mg Vitamin E + bone-critical Ca, Mg, Vitamin K per 100 g

Joint and mineral support powerhouse — rich in Calcium and Magnesium for bone strength.

Key Compound

Vitamin K + Calcium + Magnesium (joint & bone matrix triad)

Select Size

Why Bok Choy?

Joint & Mineral SupportCalcium & MagnesiumBone strengthRecovery support

How to Consume

  • •Best consumed raw — mild flavour makes it easy to add to smoothies, salads, or as a rice bowl topper
  • •The Ca + Mg + Vitamin K triad in bok choy makes it specifically excellent for bone and joint health
  • •30 g with a meal provides a meaningful share of daily Vitamin A and C requirements
  • •Pairs particularly well with basil microgreens for a stress + joint recovery combination

Key Bioactives

Glucosinolates → Sulforaphane (Brassica family)

Bok choy, as a Brassica rapa, contains glucosinolates that convert to sulforaphane — supporting liver detox and anti-inflammatory pathways

💡 Lower glucosinolate density than broccoli but still meaningful; eat raw for best bioavailability

Indole-3-carbinol (I3C)

Brassica-specific compound with documented oestrogen-metabolism modulating activity; studied for cancer prevention (breast, cervical)

β-carotene + Lutein + Zeaxanthin

Comprehensive carotenoid profile supporting eye health, immune function, and skin integrity

DPPH Antioxidant Capacity

160.1 µmol Trolox equivalent/100 g FW (peer-reviewed measurement) — solid antioxidant profile for a mild-flavoured green

Folate + Vitamin B6

Together these B-vitamins reduce homocysteine build-up — high homocysteine is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease and joint inflammation
